item.title: Self-Hosted Service Discovery and Coordination: Consul vs etcd vs ZooKeeper
item.description: Modern distributed systems depend on service discovery and coordination to function reliably. When microservices need to find each other, when distributed locks prevent race conditions, and when configuration changes must propagate instantly across a cluster, a coordination backend becomes essential infrastructure. This guide compares three battle-tested open-source coordination systems: HashiCorp Consul, etcd (the Kubernetes backbone), and Apache ZooKeeper.

item.title: Self-Hosted Distributed Locking: etcd vs ZooKeeper vs Consul vs Redis 2026
item.description: When multiple services need coordinated access to a shared resource, a distributed lock is the answer. Whether you’re running scheduled jobs across kubernetes pods, managing leader election in a microservices cluster, or preventing double-processing in a distributed queue, picking the right locking primitive matters.
